How corroboration is counted and recorded

Source: vignettes/corroboration-ledger.Rmd
corroboration-ledger.Rmd

vignette("corroborators") explains what n_corroborators means and how to choose a threshold. This vignette explains how the count is made:

  • where each filer’s statement is stored;
  • how the statements become one row in name;
  • how the guards read the same rows;
  • what happens to the count when a new release arrives.

The figures are from the build of 2026-11-01 (matchdb@df7e2ce, normalizer v1-592912060053c4c3).

Who says what

Most of what matchdb holds is first-party: the IRS or the organization itself, in the BMF, a 990 header, a 1023-EZ, an e-Postcard. A first-party name is corroborated by time. A name an organization files under for ten years has n_periods = 10.

An observed name is written by a third party, next to the EIN it is about. Three sources do this. Each is a mentions source (md_source_kinds()): one filer can write about an EIN as often as it likes, and every time is kept.

source where observations filers EINs written about
schedi Schedule I Part II: a grantmaker’s US grantees 8,798,053 93,953 823,481
efile_related Schedule R Part II: related exempt organizations 6,389,480 94,071 121,853
efile_affiliate_listing the group-return roster: a central organization’s subordinates 28,850 341 7,845

Each observation records who wrote it: the filer’s EIN, as asserted_by. That one column is what corroboration counts.

The ledger

Every observation from every source is one row in the observation ledger. Rows are never deleted or overwritten. Three tables hold it:

table one row per what it holds
release file read: a source, a version and a part, which is a tax year for e-file sources file_md5, n_rows, seq (the order of application), ingested_at
obs observation ein, role, name_text_id, address_text_id, asserted_by, period (the tax year), record_key (the return), first_release, last_release, retracted_in
name_text, address_text distinct string the string as written, keyed by a content hash

The ledger holds 48.3M observations from 82 releases. Schedule I alone is 17 releases, one for each tax year from 2009 to 2025.

The ledger is in the maintainer copy only. MATCHDB-full.duckdb (24.2 GB) has it. MATCHDB.duckdb (11.8 GB), which md_fetch_db() downloads, keeps the rollups built from it, described below. To read the ledger, download the full copy from the same location (md_remote()).

One observation holds a name and an address together when the filer wrote them together. Here is every Schedule I statement about one EIN, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Boston, as the ledger has them (first rows):

con <- md_db(read_only = TRUE, path = "MATCHDB-full.duckdb")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT o.asserted_by, o.period, t.name_raw, o.record_key
  FROM obs o JOIN name_text t USING (name_text_id)
  WHERE o.ein = 'EIN-04-2994233' AND o.role = 'observed'
  ORDER BY t.name_raw, o.asserted_by, o.period")
#>      asserted_by period                    name_raw             record_key
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2016       Bangor HFH of Greater OID-201713259349300911
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2016         Bennington Area HFH OID-201713259349300911
#>   EIN-68-0480736   2010 Boston Habitat for Humanity OID-201121809349300617
#>   EIN-68-0480736   2011 Boston Habitat for Humanity OID-201221819349300232
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2009      GREATER BOSTON INC HFH OID-201140539349300109
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2011      GREATER BOSTON INC HFH OID-201203569349300870
#>   ...
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2020      GREATER BOSTON INC HFH OID-202143379349300209
#>   EIN-91-1914868   2020      GREATER BOSTON INC HFH OID-202133199349308053
#>   ...

record_key is the return the statement came from, so any count below can be traced back to the filings behind it.

From statements to a name row

name is rebuilt from the ledger on every build; it is never edited in place. Statements are grouped by EIN, source and class, and by the name’s light key (md_light_key(): uppercased, accents and & spelled out, punctuation dropped). So Boston Habitat for Humanity and BOSTON HABITAT FOR HUMANITY are one group. Each group becomes one row:

column how it is counted
n_corroborators distinct asserted_by: how many different filers wrote it
n_mentions statements, counting each filer’s latest return for a tax year once
n_periods distinct tax years it was written in
first_year, last_year the first and last of those years
name_raw the group’s most frequent spelling, ties broken alphabetically, so a rebuild picks the same one
n_self_filers, filer_ein_lo, filer_ein_hi how many filers wrote their own EIN, and the range of the others; the guards read these

The same EIN’s rows in name:

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT name_raw, source, n_corroborators, n_mentions, n_periods, first_year, last_year
  FROM name WHERE ein = 'EIN-04-2994233'
  ORDER BY variant_class, n_corroborators DESC NULLS LAST")
#>                                  name_raw   source n_corroborators n_mentions n_periods first_year last_year
#>                    HFH GREATER BOSTON INC      bmf              NA          0         0         NA        NA
#>   HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON INC efile990              NA          0        16       2009      2024
#>       HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON   schedi              10         17         9       2012      2024
#>   HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON INC   schedi               9         34        13       2012      2025
#>    HABITAT FOR HUMANITY INTERNATIONAL INC   schedi               5         25        11       2014      2024
#>                      HABITAT FOR HUMANITY   schedi               2          3         3       2021      2024
#>                    GREATER BOSTON INC HFH   schedi               1          9         9       2009      2024
#>                       Bennington Area HFH   schedi               1          1         1       2016      2016
#>   ...

Three things to read in it:

  • Repetition by one filer is not corroboration. GREATER BOSTON INC HFH was written in nine years, every time by the same filer (EIN-91-1914868): 9 mentions, 1 corroborator. That filer sent two 2020 returns, and only the later one counts.
  • Agreement across filers is. Ten different grantmakers wrote HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON. That is the name a grant record is likely to carry, and the BMF’s HFH GREATER BOSTON INC is not.
  • A single filer can simply be wrong. The filer that wrote GREATER BOSTON INC HFH also wrote Bennington Area HFH and Bangor HFH of Greater under this EIN, in the same 2016 return. Those are other affiliates, given the wrong EIN. min_corroborators = 2 leaves them out without anyone having to find them.

The BMF row has n_corroborators = NA, not 0. First-party rows have no asserted_by, so the count does not apply to them.

Addresses travel with their names

A grantmaker writes a name and an address together, and the rollup keeps the pair. Each observed address row carries the name_id of the name it was written with:

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT a.street_raw, a.city_raw, a.zip5, a.n_corroborators, n.name_raw AS written_with
  FROM address a LEFT JOIN name n ON n.name_id = a.name_id
  WHERE a.ein = 'EIN-04-2994233' AND a.variant_class = 'observed'
  ORDER BY a.n_corroborators DESC")
#>                         street_raw city_raw  zip5 n_corroborators                            written_with
#>    240 Commercial Street 4th Floor   Boston 02109               7 HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON INC
#>    240 COMMERCIAL STREET 4TH FLOOR   BOSTON 02109               6     HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON
#> 434 MASSACHUSETTS AVENUE SUITE 201   BOSTON 02118               5     HABITAT FOR HUMANITY GREATER BOSTON
#>   ...

An observed address is counted the same way: distinct filers who wrote that place with that name. It is grouped on the name, city, state and ZIP, keeping the commonest street spelling. Grouping on the street as well would have split one grantee’s place into a row per spelling. A compiled reference therefore pairs each alias with its own addresses, about k + m rows for an EIN with k names and m addresses, not k × m.

What the guards add

Corroboration asks how many filers agree. Some errors are habits, and habits repeat across filers. md_guard_observed() reads the same rows and flags, without deleting:

  • the placeholder EINs and names;
  • the filer’s own EIN written for a grantee;
  • a group central’s EIN written for one of its members;
  • a fiscal sponsor’s EIN written for many projects.

vignette("corroborators") lists the flags. Guarded observed names, build of 2026-11-01:

source observed names placeholder EIN placeholder name own EIN group central many names any
schedi 1,767,331 13,489 149 5,892 12,551 60,703 73,949
schedr 187,999 704 55 599 229 1,067 2,054
efile990 (rosters) 9,479 0 1 0 1 0 2

md_compile() always leaves guard_any rows out of a reference. The two checks cover different errors:

  • a name written once, by mistake, is low on corroboration and usually unflagged;
  • a central’s EIN written for its congregations is often highly corroborated, and flagged.

From a name row to a reference

md_spec(min_corroborators =) keeps observed rows at or above the threshold. It must be a band edge (1, 2, 5 or 20) because the corpus statistics (name_freq, token_idf) are precomputed per layer, class and band (md_build_stats()) and summed at compile time.

When several rows normalize to one name_key for an EIN (two spellings, or two sources), the compiled row takes the largest n_corroborators among them. When a spec caps the names per class (max_names), the most corroborated names are kept first.

When a new release arrives

Statements are only ever added to the ledger. When a source publishes a new release, md_apply_release() compares it with what the ledger already holds for the same source and partition:

  • new statements are inserted;
  • statements still there have their last_release moved forward;
  • statements the publisher withdrew are marked retracted_in, never deleted. None have been withdrawn so far.

Then name and address are rebuilt from the whole ledger, so every count above is recomputed from scratch. A new tax year of Schedule I can raise a name’s n_corroborators and move it into a higher band. It can also bring a first corroborator, so that a name starts out at one filer and only later appears in the *-observed tiers. Because the counts are rebuilt, not incremented, a rebuild from the same releases always gives the same counts.

vignette("updates") describes the whole update, from a new source release to published references.

md_db_close(con)
